title: iPhone 5S review | The Verge
quote: For $199 plus a two-year contract, the 5S is Apple at its swaggering best, believing it can win the spec-sheet arms race while still offering a device anyone and everyone can use.

title: iPhone 5s review
quote: Though it's easy to dismiss this handset as iterative, the 5s is the first smartphone with full 64-bit support and a capacitive fingerprint sensor, and it also ships with a fresh, revamped version of iOS.

title: Same look, small screen, big potential - CNET
quote: Bottom line: The iPhone 5S is not a required upgrade, but it’s easily the fastest and most advanced Apple smartphone to date.

title: Nexus 5 review | The Verge
quote: The Nexus 5 is stacked in the hardware department, touts a handful of future-facing improvements, and most importantly runs the latest version of Android — a visual and functional upgrade called KitKat (or 4.4, if you love numbers). It’s a big deal.

title: A Nexus with power, potential, and the right price - CNET
quote: Bottom line: Strong performance, high-end specs, and an ultra-affordable price make the Google Nexus 5 not just the best unlocked phone on the market, but the best Nexus phone by far.

title: Google Nexus 5 review | TechRadar
quote: There's a minimalist charm to the Nexus 5 that's hard to resist. It's comfortable to hold, the display looks great, it's extremely fast, and it never slips up or stutters. This is Google's invitingly priced vision of a premium Android smartphone.

title: Nvidia Shield Tablet Review | PCMag
quote: Nvidia's gaming-oriented Shield Tablet is one of the first mobile devices to use the Tegra K1 CPU, and in sheer power it blows other tablets out of the water.

title: NVIDIA Shield tablet review: a solid slate with a gaming addiction
quote: Specifically, the Shield tablet is a $299 8-inch gaming slate powered by NVIDIA's new Tegra K1 processor.

title: An Android gaming tablet with benefits - CNET
quote: Bottom line: Even if you don’t take advantage of its gaming prowess, the Nvidia Shield Tablet is one of the most versatile — and affordable — high-performance 8-inch Android slates you can buy.

title: iPhone 6 review | The Verge
quote: It’s the iPhone 6: a bigger, brighter, badder iPhone designed to appeal to the customers for whom the iPhone 5S and its 4-inch screen now seem adorably antiquated.

title: iPhone 6 sets the smartphone bar - CNET
quote: Bottom line: The iPhone 6 is an exceptional phone in nearly every way except its average battery life: it’s thin, fast, and features the excellent iOS operating system. It was the best overall phone introduced in 2014.

title: iPhone 6 and 6 Plus review: bigger and better, but with stiffer competition
quote: With the 4.7-inch iPhone 6 and the 5.5-inch iPhone 6 Plus, the company introduced two new high-end phones at the same time, both with a complete redesign and a much larger screen size than any iPhone that came before.

title: Xbox One X review | The Verge
quote: It’s a smaller, sleeker, faster console than the original, and it’s easily more capable than the PS4 or PS4 Pro (Sony’s 4K console) in terms of raw power.

title: Xbox One X review: A console that keeps up with gaming PCs
quote: And it plays more titles in native 4K than Sony's PlayStation 4 Pro. It's just about everything you could want without investing in a gaming PC.

title: Xbox One X Review - IGN
quote: The Xbox One X is a very impressive collection of hardware crammed into a sleek case. It runs cool and quiet as it delivers performance a step above any of its console competitors.

title: PSVR 2 review: love on a leash | The Verge
quote: It’s the first consumer headset to offer eye tracking and the first to arguably offer PC-quality VR without a PC.

title: PlayStation VR2 Review - IGN
quote: It’s a thrill when we get to say this about a new piece of gaming hardware: The PlayStation VR 2 is a true generational leap that makes the old one look like a piece of junk.

title: PlayStation VR2 review: A great headset that should be cheaper
quote: The PlayStation VR2 is the virtual reality upgrade console gamers have been waiting for — but is it really worth $550? That depends on how much you need high quality VR.
